claims.text: The as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy has a coarse eutectic microstructure.
Controlled post-casting thermal annealing can refine the eutectic lamellae.
Controlled post-casting thermal annealing can promote beneficial secondary precipitate formation.
The proposed treatment produces a hierarchical microstructure with narrower eutectic lamellae.
The proposed treatment may produce fine secondary phases at eutectic interfaces.
Reduced eutectic lamellar spacing increases dislocation blocking.
Increased dislocation blocking enhances yield strength.
The refined microstructure promotes more uniform plastic deformation.
The refined microstructure delays crack initiation.
More uniform plastic deformation and delayed crack initiation improve tensile ductility.
At room temperature and moderate strain rates, the annealed alloy will exhibit a statistically significant increase of more than 10% in yield strength relative to the as-cast alloy.
At room temperature and moderate strain rates, the annealed alloy will exhibit a statistically significant increase of more than 10% in tensile ductility relative to the as-cast alloy.
The simultaneous strength–ductility improvement requires alloys with well-defined eutectic phases.
The simultaneous strength–ductility improvement requires annealing conditions that avoid over-aging or microstructural coarsening.
Excessive annealing temperature or duration may eliminate the beneficial strength and ductility effects.
